ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB$ is the diameter of the circle $\odot O$ with $AB=26$, and point $C$ is a point on the semicircle of $\odot O$. $CE \perp AB$ at point $E$, the angle bisector of $\angle OCE$ intersects $\odot O$ at point $D$, and the chord $AC=10$. What is the area of the triangle $\triangle ACD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect OD and draw AF $\perp$ CD with the foot at F, \\
$\because$ AB is the diameter of $\odot$O, \\
$\therefore \angle ACB=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ACE+\angle ECB=90^\circ$, \\
$\because CE\perp AB$, \\
$\therefore \angle CEB=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle CBE+\angle ECB=90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ACE=\angle CBE$, \\
$\because OB=OC$, \\
$\therefore \angle CBE=\angle OCB$, \\
$\therefore \angle ACE=\angle OCB$, \\
$\because CD$ bisects $\angle OCE$, \\
$\therefore \angle OCD=\angle ECD$, \\
$\therefore \angle ACE+\angle DCE=\angle OCB+\angle OCD= \frac{1}{2} \angle ACB=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle ACD=45^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle AOD=2\angle ACD=90^\circ$, \\
In $\triangle ACF$, AC=10, \\
$\therefore AF=AC\cdot\sin45^\circ=10\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} =5\sqrt{2}$, \\
$CF=AC\cdot\cos45^\circ=10\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} =5\sqrt{2}$, \\
In $\triangle AOD$, AO=OD=$\frac{1}{2}$AB=13, \\
$\therefore AD=\sqrt{2}AO=13\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore DF=\sqrt{AD^2-AF^2}=\sqrt{(13\sqrt{2})^2-(5\sqrt{2})^2}=12\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore CD=CF+DF=17\sqrt{2}$, \\
$\therefore$ the area of $\triangle ACD$= $\frac{1}{2}$CD$\cdot$AF\\
= $\frac{1}{2}\times17\sqrt{2}\times5\sqrt{2}$\\
= $\boxed{85}$.
